questions.question_text: Which of the following describes blunting of affect?

options.text: Inability to show reactivity of affect
Insensitivity to the subtleties of social intercourse
Limitation in the usual range of emotional responses

correct_answer.text: Insensitivity to the subtleties of social intercourse

correct_answers.text: Insensitivity to the subtleties of social intercourse

questions.explanation: Blunting of affect refers to a lack of emotional responsiveness, creating situations where patients are indifferent to their wellbeing and that of others.

questions.question_text: According to the International Classification of Disease, 10th revision (ICD-10), which of the following is a criterion for an adjustment disorder?

options.text: The patient continues to function normally
The symptoms must occur within 1 month of an identifiable psychosocial stressor
The symptoms persist longer than 6 months in all types of manifestations
There is a correlation with drug-related problems
The disorder category includes separation anxiety disorder of childhood

correct_answer.text: The symptoms must occur within 1 month of an identifiable psychosocial stressor

correct_answers.text: The symptoms must occur within 1 month of an identifiable psychosocial stressor

questions.explanation: Adjustment disorder is characterized by the onset of symptoms occurring within one month of a psychosocial stressor.

questions.question_text: While administering the mini-mental state examination (MMSE) to a 78-year-old man, he asked you what is being assessed by copying the diagram of interlocking pentagons. What would you say to him?
questions.explanation: Copying the diagram assesses constructional praxis, which evaluates a patient's ability to construct and organize visual information.

questions.question_text: Over a period of 18 months, a 41-year-old man developed clumsiness, unsteady gait and poverty of speech. He appeared apathetic, depressed and paranoid. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The address test assesses short-term memory impairment, which is consistent with the described symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct with regard to eliciting information from patients?

options.text: Closed questions are the least frequent causes of interruption
Most patients are allowed to complete their opening statement
Most patients present their problems in a logical order
Most patients take less than 2 minutes to complete their opening statement
The longer the clinician waited, the less information was elicited

correct_answer.text: Most patients take less than 2 minutes to complete their opening statement

correct_answers.text: Most patients take less than 2 minutes to complete their opening statement

questions.explanation: Most patients complete their opening statement within 2 minutes, and studies show this is the typical length of time.

questions.question_text: The family of a 41-year-old man was concerned that over the past 18 months he had become clumsy and unsteady while walking. He appeared apathetic, depressed and paranoid. His thoughts have slowed down. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms described, including clumsiness and changes in behavior, point towards a diagnosis of Huntington's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of an open question?

options.text: Has your sleep been poor recently?
Have you been feeling depressed recently?
Have you lost any weight recently?
Have you lost pleasures in things recently?
How have you been feeling in your spirits recently?

correct_answer.text: How have you been feeling in your spirits recently?

correct_answers.text: How have you been feeling in your spirits recently?

questions.explanation: Open questions, like this one, allow the patient to elaborate and provide a more qualitative response.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive functions is assessed by the serial sevens test?
questions.explanation: The serial sevens test specifically measures concentration as the participant counts backwards by sevens.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most accurate statement about the use of the MMSE in the assessment of a patient with suspected dementia?

options.text: A score of <23 is diagnostic of Alzheimer's disease
An average patient with untreated Alzheimer's disease will lose 3–4 points per year
MMSE has a high sensitivity for detecting language difficulties
Persevering on items that the patient finds difficult usually gives the best results
The scores correlate highly with detailed neuropsychological tests

correct_answer.text: An average patient with untreated Alzheimer's disease will lose 3–4 points per year

correct_answers.text: An average patient with untreated Alzheimer's disease will lose 3–4 points per year

questions.explanation: On average, untreated Alzheimer's patients lose about 3-4 points on the MMSE each year.

questions.question_text: A 78-year-old man was brought to the accident and emergency department after being found wandering about during the night. During his assessment, which of the following will help the clinician to distinguish between delirium and dementia?
questions.explanation: Impaired consciousness is a key characteristic of delirium, differentiating it from dementia.

questions.question_text: Most of the neuropsychological tests do not allow one to guess. Which of the following test results is based on how much a patient can actually guess?
questions.explanation: The cognitive estimates test allows guessing, while other neuropsychological tests do not.

questions.question_text: What is the 'map search' test used to assess?

options.text: The visuospatial ability of a person

questions.explanation: The map search test evaluates the speed of processing information.

questions.question_text: Which part of the brain is assessed by the trail-making test?
questions.explanation: The trail-making test assesses the functioning of the frontal lobes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cognitive dysfunction in schizophrenia is correct?

options.text: All individuals who develop schizophrenia have a cognitive dysfunction
Impaired cognitive test performance in patients with schizophrenia is an epiphenomenon
Low IQ at a young age is a risk factor for schizophrenia
Schizophrenia does not cause intellectual decline
Visuospatial memory functioning is a predictor of functional outcome in schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Low IQ at a young age is a risk factor for schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Low IQ at a young age is a risk factor for schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Research indicates that having a low IQ in childhood can be a risk factor for developing schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of the amnestic syndrome?

options.text: Loss of memory of the period before the brain damage

questions.explanation: The amnestic syndrome is characterized by significant memory impairment while immediate memory typically remains intact.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neuropsychological tests is found to be accurate in differentiating Alzheimer's disease from depressive pseudodementia?
questions.explanation: The paired associative learning test can reliably differentiate between Alzheimer's disease and pseudodementia.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old man complained of an inability to see in the upper left corner of his vision. On examination, you found a visual field defect in the left upper quadrant of both eyes. Where is the lesion likely to be located in the brain?
questions.explanation: A right occipital lobe lesion would cause a defect in the left upper quadrant of the visual field due to the visual pathway's processing.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old woman gave a history of intermittent numbness, tingling in her limbs and visual impairment. On eye examination, you noticed that, on attempted left lateral gaze, the right eye failed to adduct and the left eye developed coarse nystagmus in abduction. What is the most likely reason for this abnormality of eye movement?
questions.explanation: The described eye movement abnormality is consistent with left internuclear ophthalmoplegia caused by a lesion in the medial longitudinal fasciculus.

questions.question_text: Your consultant has informed you that a patient who was recently assessed has Bell's palsy, with a lesion in the petrous temporal bone. Which of the following clinical features would indicate the origin of the lesion?

options.text: Corneal ulceration on the affected side
Failure of conjugate lateral gaze (towards the lesion)
Loss of taste on the posterior third of the tongue
Normal furrowing of the brow on the same side as the lesion

questions.explanation: Bell's palsy affecting the petrous temporal bone leads to hyperacusis due to the involvement of the stapedius muscle.

questions.question_text: You examined a patient with multi-infarct dementia. From your examination findings, you concluded that he had developed pseudobulbar palsy. Which of the following is consistent with this diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Dysarthria is a common feature of pseudobulbar palsy due to the affected control of motor speech.

questions.question_text: A 76-year-old woman complained of mild memory loss, mental and physical slowing, and difficulty in thinking for the past 6 months. On examination, she has a broad-based shuffling gait and a diagnosis of normal pressure hydrocephalus is considered. Which of the following features will help you to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Urinary incontinence is one of the classic triad of symptoms associated with normal pressure hydrocephalus.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old man with epilepsy and a mild learning disability is brought to the accident and emergency department with aggressive behavior; he has also been found wandering on the street. He is taking carbamazepine, lithium and zopiclone. Which of the following will help you to understand the possible cause of his presentation?
questions.explanation: An electroencephalogram (EEG) can help identify seizure activity that could explain the patient's aggressive behavior.

questions.question_text: A 50-year-old widow is admitted with confusion and aggressive behavior of recent origin. She is known to have renal failure and depression, for which she takes paroxetine. Which of the following will help you understand the possible cause of her presentation?
questions.explanation: Measuring the serum paroxetine level can help assess its effect and possible toxicity in the context of renal failure.

questions.question_text: A 39-year-old man with chronic schizophrenia complained of a sore throat and fever. He was diagnosed as having MRSA during his previous admission to the medical ward. He had been taking clozapine for the past 2 years. Which of the following will help you understand the possible cause of his current problem?
questions.explanation: A full blood count helps monitor for clozapine-induced agranulocytosis and infection.

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old man is considering an application for a university course. However, he has a weak academic record in his school studies. He is regarded as outgoing, level-headed, happy and well-adjusted, with no previous history of behavioral or emotional difficulties. In response to a referral from his general practitioner, which psychological instrument will be most appropriate in assessing this person?
questions.explanation: The Wechsler adult intelligence scale is appropriate for assessing cognitive capabilities in a university applicant.

questions.question_text: A 58-year-old chief executive of a National Health Service trust experienced a brief period of mild right-sided paraesthesia and a left-sided headache of 12 hours' duration. After 1 week, he saw his neurologist who observed forgetfulness, decreased understanding of complex information and diminished daily living skills. Which of the following is the most appropriate test in assessing this man?
questions.explanation: The Halstead–Reitan battery is suitable for detailed neuropsychological assessment given the reported symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old single man with a narcissistic personality disorder had received insight-oriented psychotherapy for 1 year. The therapist felt that there has been little or no progress in the therapy for several months. Which of the following tests is most likely to reveal the personality dynamics that might be helpful in understanding the therapeutic impasse?
questions.explanation: Rorschach's inkblot technique can provide insights into personality dynamics relevant for therapeutic understanding.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is recognized as a poor prognostic factor in anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Childhood obesity is associated with a poorer outcome in cases of anorexia nervosa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common comorbidity associated with a panic disorder?
questions.explanation: Depression is the most common comorbidity seen in individuals with panic disorder.

questions.question_text: A 15-year-old girl presented with a history of dieting and excessive exercising. Her height is 165 cm and current weight 50 kg. What is her body mass index?

options.text: Below the cut-off to diagnose anorexia nervosa

questions.explanation: Her BMI is approximately 18.4, which falls between 18 and 19, indicating a normal range.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common neuroendocrine change found in patients with anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Delayed insulin release is one of the neuroendocrine changes noted in patients with anorexia nervosa.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old man informed you that he was a heavy user of cannabis. He was seeking advice about the risks associated with cannabis use. What would you tell him?

options.text: Cannabis use can precipitate schizophrenia in people who are vulnerable because of a family history of the disorder
Chronic cannabis use has no effect on motivation and social performance
Long-term cannabis use causes physical dependence
Long-term cannabis use causes severe cognitive impairment
Long-term cannabis use does not cause tolerance

correct_answer.text: Cannabis use can precipitate schizophrenia in people who are vulnerable because of a family history of the disorder

correct_answers.text: Cannabis use can precipitate schizophrenia in people who are vulnerable because of a family history of the disorder

questions.explanation: Cannabis use has been linked to the development of schizophrenia in individuals with a genetic predisposition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best predictor of long-term general intellectual impairment after a head injury?

options.text: Glasgow Coma Scale score on admission

questions.explanation: The duration of post-traumatic amnesia is a strong predictor of long-term cognitive outcomes following head injury.

questions.question_text: If a person starts smoking cannabis before the age of 15 years, what is the chance of developing a psychotic disorder before the age of 26 years?
questions.explanation: Research shows that starting cannabis use before age 15 increases the risk of developing a psychotic disorder by four times.

questions.question_text: What is the prevalence of major depression in older people with congestive cardiac failure compared with cardiac patients with no heart failure?
questions.explanation: The prevalence of major depression is found to be roughly 2:1 in older patients with congestive heart failure compared to those without.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is associated with negative symptoms of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Studies suggest that negative symptoms in schizophrenia are related to hypofunction in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.

questions.question_text: A 69-year-old retired banker underwent major abdominal surgery. Three days later, he was noticed to be agitated, restless, confused and visually hallucinated. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms following surgery are indicative of delirium, particularly given the recent change in mental status.

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old woman presented with a gradual reduction in her verbal fluency, motivation and self-control. She also exhibited a degree of disinhibition. Her EEG was normal. Which of the following best describes her condition?
questions.explanation: Her symptoms are consistent with frontotemporal dementia, characterized by changes in personality and behavior.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a part of the diagnostic criteria for emotionally unstable personality disorder, according to the ICD-10?

options.text: Involvement in intense and unstable relationships
Recurrent threats or acts of self-harm

questions.explanation: Transient stress-related paranoid ideation is not included as a diagnostic criterion for emotionally unstable personality disorder in ICD-10.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old man was recently reviewed in the emergency department due to an increase in recent bouts of verbal aggression. He did not make any eye contact, continued to talk over the practitioner and was difficult to interrupt. He preferred his own company and had a rigid routine and a keen interest in collecting models of fighter planes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The described behaviors are consistent with high functioning autism, characterized by social difficulties and fixed interests.

questions.question_text: A 19-year-old man was seen in an outpatient clinic after a referral from his general practitioner due to a long-term problem with concentration. On examination, he exhibited an abundance of thoughts which shifted from one task to another and a tendency to act impulsively without thinking through the consequences of his actions. He mentioned that he had lots of energy, his bedroom was in disarray and at work he would stop working on projects once the challenging part was over. He easily became bored with things and did not pay much attention to details. He easily misplaced and lost things. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms described suggest a hyperkinetic disorder, which is often associated with inattention and impulsiveness.

questions.question_text: Which pair of clinical features is most likely to be present in persistent delusional disorder?

options.text: Bizarre encapsulated delusions and systematised delusions
Blunting of affect and delusions of control
Mood congruent delusions and prominent affective symptoms
Persistent auditory hallucinations and definite evidence of brain disease
Prominent depressive symptoms and persecutory delusions

correct_answer.text: Bizarre encapsulated delusions and systematised delusions

correct_answers.text: Bizarre encapsulated delusions and systematised delusions

questions.explanation: Persistent delusional disorder is characterized by well-formed delusions that may be bizarre or systematic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is characteristic of the ICD-10 diagnostic hierarchy?

options.text: Any given diagnosis includes the presence of all the symptoms of higher members of the hierarchy
ICD-9 and ICD-10 have the same hierarchical structure
Neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders are in the middle of the hierarchy
Organic disorders are at the bottom of the hierarchy
Schizophrenia and affective disorders are at the same level

correct_answer.text: Schizophrenia and affective disorders are at the same level

correct_answers.text: Schizophrenia and affective disorders are at the same level

questions.explanation: In ICD-10, schizophrenia and affective disorders are placed at the same level in the diagnostic hierarchy.

questions.question_text: In some cases of schizophrenia, the ICD-10 allows coding of a fifth character. What does this fifth character signify?
questions.explanation: The fifth character can be used to specify the pattern of the course of schizophrenia, which may vary over time.

questions.question_text: In the ICD-10, under which category is multiple personality disorder classified?

options.text: Enduring personality changes, not attributable to brain damage and disease

questions.explanation: Multiple personality disorder is classified under dissociative disorders in the ICD-10.

questions.question_text: According to the ICD-10, which of the following categories includes paedophilia?

options.text: Other disorders such as adult personality and behaviour disorders
Psychological and behaviour disorders associated with sexual development and orientation

questions.explanation: Paedophilia is classified under disorders of sexual preferences in the ICD-10.

questions.question_text: According to the ICD-10, which of the following categories includes the schizotypal disorder?
questions.explanation: Schizotypal disorder is classified as a personality disorder in the ICD-10.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is included under schizophrenia in the ICD-10? AI chose E
questions.explanation: Schizoaffective disorder is classified under schizophrenia and related disorders in the ICD-10.

questions.question_text: According to the ICD-10, what is the minimum duration for symptoms of obsession and compulsion to persist in order to meet the criteria of obsessive–compulsive disorder?
questions.explanation: Symptoms must persist for at least two successive weeks to meet the criteria for obsessive–compulsive disorder according to ICD-10.

questions.question_text: According to the ICD-10, what is the minimum duration of symptoms to meet the criteria for generalised anxiety disorder?
questions.explanation: Symptoms of generalised anxiety disorder must be present for at least 6 months for a diagnosis according to ICD-10.

questions.question_text: In which of the following classification systems is a diagnosis of narcissistic personality disorder included?

options.text: Both the ICD-10 and the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th edn (DSM-IV)

questions.explanation: Narcissistic personality disorder is classified in the DSM-IV but is not included in the ICD-10.

questions.question_text: What is the duration of symptoms that meets the diagnostic criteria for somatisation disorder in the ICD-10?
questions.explanation: The features of somatisation disorder (Briquet’s syndrome) are multiple, recurrent and frequently changing symptoms spread over 2 years. The symptoms emanate from multiple systems of the body. It is supported by negative investigations and several unremarkable exploratory operations might have been performed.

questions.question_text: What is the duration of symptoms that meets the diagnostic criteria of delusional disorders in the ICD-10?
questions.explanation: Delusional disorders must have persistent symptoms for at least 3 months according to the ICD-10.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the properties of trazodone is correct?

options.text: It inhibits monoamine oxidase enzymes A and B
It is relatively safe in overdose

correct_answer.text: It is relatively safe in overdose

correct_answers.text: It is relatively safe in overdose

questions.explanation: Trazodone is generally considered to be relatively safe in overdose compared to other antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the properties of donepezil is correct?

options.text: It blocks the damaging effects of normal excitotoxicity
It is a non-competitive, reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase
It potentiates the action of acetylcholine at the nicotinic receptors

correct_answer.text: It is a non-competitive, reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase

correct_answers.text: It is a non-competitive, reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase

questions.explanation: Donepezil is a reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase, which increases acetylcholine levels.

questions.question_text: You have assessed a 10-year-old boy, with diagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, who presents with complaints of severe abdominal pain. He has not taken his medication methylphenidate and clonidine since he ran away from home 2 days ago. He has undergone an extensive physical examination, drug tests and investigations, which proved negative. What is the most likely cause of his abdominal pain?
questions.explanation: Clonidine withdrawal can lead to a range of physical symptoms, including abdominal pain.

questions.question_text: What is the mode of action of atomoxetine in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder?
questions.explanation: Atomoxetine is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that is used to treat ADHD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a triazolopyridine?
questions.explanation: Trazodone is classified as a triazolopyridine antidepressant.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a tertiary amine?
questions.explanation: Amitriptyline is classified as a tertiary amine antidepressant.

questions.question_text: Many of the psychotropic drugs can cause priapism. Which of the following is the mechanism for priapism?
questions.explanation: Priapism occurs as a result of α1-receptor blockade, leading to smooth muscle tone dysregulation.

questions.question_text: Fluvoxamine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. Which of the following receptors does it act on to improve cognition and depression?
questions.explanation: Fluvoxamine acts as a sigma-1 receptor agonist in the brain, aiding in cognition and depressive symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for developing a rash with lamotrigine therapy?

options.text: Exceeding the rate of the recommended dose escalation

correct_answer.text: Exceeding the rate of the recommended dose escalation

correct_answers.text: Exceeding the rate of the recommended dose escalation

questions.explanation: Exceeding the recommended rate of dose escalation with lamotrigine increases the risk of serious rash.

questions.question_text: For the past 2 years, a 42-year-old woman has been prescribed an antiepileptic medication as a mood stabiliser for the treatment of bipolar affective disorder. She has recently developed renal stones. Which antiepileptic drug is likely to have caused this problem?
questions.explanation: Topiramate has been associated with the development of renal stones as a side effect.

questions.question_text: A 46-year-old woman is prescribed an antiepileptic drug as a mood stabiliser for the treatment of bipolar affective disorder. She complains of tunnel vision. Which of the following is likely to be the drug involved in this side effect?
questions.explanation: Vigabatrin can cause visual field defects, including tunnel vision, due to its side effects.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old man with a history of heroin dependence attended a party and took buprenorphine supplied by a friend. Which of the following symptoms is he most likely to experience?
questions.explanation: Tachycardia is a symptom of opioid withdrawal, which can occur with buprenorphine use.

questions.question_text: A 3-year-old boy was specifically attached to his mother. He became uncomfortable when handled by other members of his family. According to Bowlby, at what age does this specific attachment start to develop in a child?
questions.explanation: Specific attachment typically develops between 6 to 9 months of age according to Bowlby's attachment theory.

questions.question_text: According to the Ainsworth strange situation experiment, a 15-month-old girl plays independently when the mother is nearby but gets distressed when she leaves the room. She then seeks contact with the mother on her return. What type of attachment behaviour is this child exhibiting?
questions.explanation: This behavior indicates secure attachment, where the child is comfortable exploring while the caregiver is present.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man gave brief answers or provided positive answers of their experiences without elaborating or explaining. According to Main's semi-structured Adult Attachment Interview, which type of attachment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Dismissing attachment is characterized by minimizing personal experience and avoiding elaboration.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman with a borderline personality disorder became highly emotional when talking about her childhood memories. She often became angry and got distressed for no apparent reason. According to Main's semi-structured Adult Attachment Interview, which type of attachment does she have?
questions.explanation: Preoccupied attachment is characterized by intense emotional reactions and difficulty regulating feelings.

questions.question_text: An infant was studied intensively and followed up at 5, 18 and 22 months. He seemed to adapt poorly to changes, had regular habits and exhibited mild intensity of emotional reactions. According to the New York Longitudinal Study, what type of behaviour does he exhibit?
questions.explanation: The described traits are characteristic of a slow to warm up temperament, involving cautiousness to new experiences.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man with alcohol dependence presents with short-term memory loss. Which of the following statements describes what is most likely to be absent?

options.text: Chunking can increase the capacity of short-term memory
Short-term memory can be extended by rehearsal
Recall of information is error free

questions.explanation: In practice, recall from short-term memory is often not error-free and may involve distortions.

questions.question_text: A 75-year-old man remembers everything about his personal history such as the day he was born, the day he got married and the day his first child was born. What type of memory does this describe?
questions.explanation: Episodic memory is the ability to remember specific events and experiences from one's own life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is untrue for sensory memory?

options.text: If attention is paid, sensory memory enters into short-term memory
Sensory memory has a short capacity

correct_answer.text: Sensory memory has a short capacity

correct_answers.text: Sensory memory has a short capacity

questions.explanation: Sensory memory has a large capacity for information but it is transient, quickly fading if not processed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is untrue for the mode for retrieval of memory?
questions.explanation: Reduction is not a recognized mode of retrieval in memory processes, while recall and recognition are standard retrieval modes.

questions.question_text: Which stage of Piaget's theory of cognitive development is associated with the pendulum experiment?
questions.explanation: The pendulum experiment is used to demonstrate abstract reasoning capabilities found in the formal operational stage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Piaget's theory of cognitive development is correct?

options.text: Castration anxiety is explained in Piaget's cognitive development
The concept of conservation and seriation develops during the preoperational stage
Deductive reasoning and hypothesis testing develop during the concrete operational stage
Object permanence is completed at 18 months

correct_answer.text: Object permanence is completed at 18 months

correct_answers.text: Object permanence is completed at 18 months

questions.explanation: Egocentrism refers to the tendency to view the world from one’s own perspective and the inability   to understand the world from other people’s points of view. Castration anxiety is associated with   the phallic stage of Freud’s psychosexual development stages, which develops between the   ages of 3 and 5 years. Abstract reasoning, logical thinking and hypothesis testing are seen in the   formal operational stage. Conservation of volume, number, length and mass is associated with the   concrete operational stage.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-old boy maintains social order and law and says 'I won't do it because it would break the law'. Which of Kohlberg's stages of moral development does this indicate?
questions.explanation: This behavior reflects Stage 4 of Kohlberg's moral development, which emphasizes maintaining social order.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with the New York Longitudinal Study of Alexander Thomas, Stella Chess and Herbert Birch?
questions.explanation: The New York Longitudinal Study focuses primarily on the study of temperament across different individuals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about memory is correct?

options.text: Memory is divided into short, intermediate and long-term types
Long-term memory is also known as secondary or remote memory
Short- and long-term memory do not differ in the amount of information that can be stored
The capacity of short-term memory is limited to 10–15 bits
Working memory and recent memory are synonymous

correct_answer.text: Long-term memory is also known as secondary or remote memory

correct_answers.text: Long-term memory is also known as secondary or remote memory

questions.explanation: Long-term memory is often referred to as secondary or remote memory, reflecting its ability to store information over lengthy periods.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is consistent with the concept of cognitive dissonance?

options.text: Attribution of an other's behaviour to situational causes
The concept is a cognitive approach
It is concerned with a person changing his or her thinking to lessen harmony
It implies incongruity in a person's beliefs, knowledge and behaviour

correct_answer.text: It implies incongruity in a person's beliefs, knowledge and behaviour

correct_answers.text: It implies incongruity in a person's beliefs, knowledge and behaviour

questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance involves experiencing discomfort due to conflicting beliefs, prompting a change to restore consonance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about learned helplessness is correct? AI chose E

options.text: By using this strategy, the individual is able to control events
Learned helplessness is a paradigm used to explain psychosis in depressed individuals
It is learning how to feign helplessness
It teaches an animal how to endure pain in order to avoid an aversive stimulus
The organism learns that no behavioural pattern can influence the environment

correct_answer.text: Learned helplessness is a paradigm used to explain psychosis in depressed individuals

correct_answers.text: Learned helplessness is a paradigm used to explain psychosis in depressed individuals

questions.explanation: Learned helplessness is a phenomenon where an organism learns that its responses have no effect on outcomes, leading to a failure to escape unpleasant situations.

questions.question_text: The new Prime Minister was sworn in after a landslide victory. He announced his cabinet soon after a sworn-in ceremony. Which of the following best describes the Prime Minister's social power to choose his cabinet as described by French and Raven?
questions.explanation: French and Raven have described five types of social power:  1. Authority/legitimate: this is the power derived from the role or positional power. Managers,   doctors and prime ministers all have legitimate power that comes with their roles.  2. Reward: this is the power derived from the ability to allocate resources. Your employer or   educational supervisor can reward you in different ways.  3. Coercive: this is the power to punish. This form forces an individual to do something against his   or her will. Think dictator, bully or parent! (It is not necessarily negative.)  4. Referent: this power is derived from another person liking you or wanting to be like you, e.g.   celebrities and local social leaders. It is being charismatic and liked by others.  5. Expert: this power is derived from skills, knowledge and experience. A trade union could enforce   this kind of power if they encouraged their members to strike for better conditions

questions.question_text: The teacher strongly believed that the charismatic union leader represented his views at the rally. Which social power, according to French and Raven, is displayed in this case?
questions.explanation: French and Raven have described the following five types of social powers:  1. Authority/Legitimate: power derived from role (as above). Managers, doctors and prime   ministers all have legitimate power that comes with their roles.  2. Reward: power derived from the ability to allocate resources. Your employer or educational   supervisor can reward you in different ways.  3. Coercive: power to punish. This is the power that forces someone to do something against his or   her will. Think dictator, bully or parent! (It is not necessarily negative.)  4. Referent: charismatic and liked by others. This power is derived from another person liking you   or wanting to be like you, e.g. celebrities and local social leaders.  5. Expert: power derives from skill, knowledge and experience. This power comes from having the   knowledge and skills that someone else requires. A trade union could enforce this kind of power   if they encouraged their members to strike for better conditions.

questions.question_text: What is the view that 'you have of yourself' called? AI chose C
questions.explanation: This scale consists of statements that have been ranked and assigned values. Patients select one   with which they agree the most and a mean score is derived. The scale is associated with bias in   ranking. Likert’s scale is a five-point scale. The semantic differential scale consists of nine or more   paired bipolar adjectives and, for each, there is a five-point visual analogue scale, on which patients   mark their response. In sociometry, patients in a group nominate preferred partners and create   sociograms, which identify subgroups.

questions.question_text: When measuring an attitude, a scale was used in which there were a large number of statements about a particular issue. Each statement had a numerical value indicating how favourable it could be. People were asked whether they agreed with each of the statements. The total number of 'agree statement' scores was averaged. Which of the following scale is being described?
questions.explanation: The Likert scale measures attitudes by allowing respondents to express the degree of their agreement with various statements.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be assessed by a vocabulary test?
questions.explanation: Vocabulary tests are commonly used to assess premorbid intelligence as they tend to remain stable over time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about a diagnostic interview is correct?

options.text: An American version of the present state examination (PSE) is called the schedule for affective disorders and schizophrenia (SADS)
PSE can be used to characterise illness
PSE provides no criteria for severity
PSE provides an operational definition of symptoms to be rated
SADS is identical to PSE in its scope of application

correct_answer.text: PSE provides an operational definition of symptoms to be rated

correct_answers.text: PSE provides an operational definition of symptoms to be rated

questions.explanation: The Present State Examination (PSE) provides an operational definition of symptoms for assessment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an observer-rated psychiatric instrument?
questions.explanation: The Present State Examination is an observer-rated instrument used to assess psychiatric symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old woman university student was assessed for behavioural therapy. Which of the following statements about behavioural therapy is correct?

options.text: Analysing life events is an integral part of the process
Concomitant use of a psychotropic drug is necessary
Functional analysis of behaviour is an absolute necessity
Operational definitions are used for behavioural patterns

correct_answer.text: Functional analysis of behaviour is an absolute necessity

correct_answers.text: Functional analysis of behaviour is an absolute necessity

questions.explanation: Behavioral therapy relies on operational definitions of behavior to assess and modify actions.

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old woman was undergoing behavioral therapy for a phobic disorder. Which of the following statements about the schedule of reinforcement is correct?

options.text: A smooth pattern of behaviour is found with a variable-ratio schedule
In a fixed-interval schedule, the rate of the responses increases in direct proportion to the duration of the interval
In a variable-ratio schedule, the rate of the response tends to be slow
The rate of response increase is found with a variable-ratio schedule

correct_answer.text: A smooth pattern of behaviour is found with a variable-ratio schedule

correct_answers.text: A smooth pattern of behaviour is found with a variable-ratio schedule

questions.explanation: Variable-ratio schedules typically produce high and steady rates of responding, often used in behavioral reinforcement.

questions.question_text: A 43-year-old male office worker was on sick leave from his work. His doctor had advised him to return to work as soon as possible. However, he was not keen to do so. He was considered to be displaying 'sick role behaviour'. Which of the following statements about this is correct?

options.text: It does not allow the patient to be exempted from normal social behaviour
It is an activity adopted by those who consider themselves to be ill
It refers to the effect of the unconscious denial
It refers to the measures taken to detect a disease in the asymptomatic stage
It refers to the measures taken to prevent a disease

correct_answer.text: It is an activity adopted by those who consider themselves to be ill

correct_answers.text: It is an activity adopted by those who consider themselves to be ill

questions.explanation: Society bestows a special role on people who are ill. Parsons (1951) termed this concept ‘sick role’,   which is made up of two privileges and two duties, as follows:  •	Exemption from certain social responsibilities  •	The right to expect help and care from others  •	The obligation to seek help and care from others  •	The expectation of a desire to recover.  When the person is ill, the sick role is adaptive. However, if the person continues in the sick role   after the illness is over, recovery is delayed as the individual continues to avoid responsibilities and   depends on others, instead of becoming independent.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman was assessed for cognitive-behavioural therapy for generalised anxiety disorder. Which of the following statements about the cognitive model of anxiety is correct?

options.text: Conditions related to real dangers are responsible for the anxiety
Interpretation of perceived loss is responsible for the anxiety
Life events are responsible for the anxiety
Patient's interpretation of life events is responsible for the anxiety
Patient's responses are appropriate to the situation in which they occur

correct_answer.text: Patient's interpretation of life events is responsible for the anxiety

correct_answers.text: Patient's interpretation of life events is responsible for the anxiety

questions.explanation: Cognitive theory proposes that generalised anxiety disorder arises from a tendency to worry   excessively and unproductively about problems, and to focus on potentially threatening   circumstances. Three kinds of cognitions are considered in the treatment.  •	Fear of fear: general concerns about the effects of being anxious, e.g. losing control.  •	Fear of symptoms: concerns about specific symptoms, e.g. fear that palpitations are a sign of   heart disease.  •	Fear of negative evaluation: concerns that other people will react unfavourably

questions.question_text: Which of the following was considered to reduce the risk of dementia but is now thought to increase the risk?
questions.explanation: Hormone replacement therapy has been found to potentially increase the risk of dementia in older women.

questions.question_text: Which of the following options has evidence for delaying the onset of Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Prolonged education is associated with a lower risk of Alzheimer's disease due to cognitive reserve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for relapse into depression during pregnancy?

options.text: Higher number of previous depressive episodes
Later age of onset of depression
Younger age of onset of depression

correct_answer.text: Higher number of previous depressive episodes

correct_answers.text: Higher number of previous depressive episodes

questions.explanation: The best predictor of the future course of depression is the history of previous episodes. Not   surprisingly, the risk of recurrence is much greater in those with several previous episodes. Other   factors include:  •	Incomplete symptomatic resolution  •	Bipolar affective disorder  •	Early age of onset  •	Poor social support  •	Poor physical health  •	Comorbid substance misuse  •	Comorbid personality disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Rose's 'preventive paradox' is correct?

options.text: Preventive measures targeted at high-risk individuals produce the best pay-off for the population
Preventive measures targeted at high-risk individuals produce the best pay-off for those individuals
Preventive measures targeted at high-risk individuals produce the best pay-off for those individuals, but the best pay-off for the population as a whole is provided by universal measures
Universal preventive measures produce the best pay-off for individuals at high risk
Universal preventive measures produce the best pay-off for individuals at low risk

correct_answer.text: Preventive measures targeted at high-risk individuals produce the best pay-off for those individuals, but the best pay-off for the population as a whole is provided by universal measures

correct_answers.text: Preventive measures targeted at high-risk individuals produce the best pay-off for those individuals, but the best pay-off for the population as a whole is provided by universal measures

questions.explanation: Rose's preventive paradox suggests that while targeted measures benefit individuals, universal measures are more effective for overall population health.

questions.question_text: You asked a 32-year-old man with schizophrenia to show his tongue and you pricked it with a pin as a part of examination. On asking him to show his tongue again, he puts his tongue out without thinking about the pinprick. How is this phenomenon best described?
questions.explanation: Automatic obedience is characterized by following commands without awareness or judgment, which is evidenced by the described behavior.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman visited a place and immediately developed a sense of familiarity because her stored memories were brought into her consciousness. How is this phenomenon best described?
questions.explanation: Déjà-vu describes the sensation of feeling an event is familiar when it is actually happening for the first time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following should not be considered for diagnosis of a delusional disorder?
questions.explanation: Delusions of control are more characteristic of schizophrenia rather than delusional disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not assessed in the MMSE?
questions.explanation: The MMSE does not directly assess apraxia; it includes tasks such as clock drawing to evaluate other cognitive functions.

questions.question_text: A 74-year-old depressed woman reported that the antiemetic drug prescribed to her had destroyed her intestines and stopped the blood flowing to her brain. She refused to eat as she believed that she no longer had any bowels. Which of the following phenomena does she describe?
questions.explanation: Cotard's syndrome is characterized by nihilistic delusions, such as believing one no longer has body parts.

questions.question_text: A general practitioner referred a 35-year-old woman to you for an assessment of obsessive–compulsive disorder. Which of the following is the most likely pattern that you would expect in this patient?

options.text: A need for symmetry or precision, which leads to a compulsion of slowness
An obsession of doubt, followed by a compulsion of checking
An obsession with dirt or germs, followed by washing or avoidance
Intrusive obsessional thoughts without a compulsion

correct_answer.text: An obsession with dirt or germs, followed by washing or avoidance

correct_answers.text: An obsession with dirt or germs, followed by washing or avoidance

questions.explanation: A common pattern in OCD is an obsession with cleanliness or contamination, resulting in compulsive washing behavior.

questions.question_text: You have assessed a 65-year-old man in your outpatient clinic. On asking him about the capital of Scotland, he answered Glasgow, on asking about the number of months in a year, he answered 14, and on asking about the colour of an orange, he answered blue. What phenomenon is he most probably displaying?
questions.explanation: Confabulation occurs when a person fills in gaps in their memory with fabricated, distorted, or misinterpreted memories without intending to deceive.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not explain the process of learning and memory?
questions.explanation: Decoding is not typically involved in the learning and memory processes, which include encoding, storage, and retrieval.

questions.question_text: A 48-year-old man with chronic schizophrenia has been on a stable dose of an antipsychotic drug for 20 years. He came to see you in clinic and frequently made a gesture similar to saluting. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.explanation: Mannerisms refer to unusual, repeated goal-directed actions, which can include gestures like saluting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be conceptualised as the déjà-vu and jamais-vu phenomena?
questions.explanation: Déjà-vu and jamais-vu are experiences related to perception, where an experience feels familiar or unfamiliar.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old white woman never left her house without covering her head in a veil. On enquiry into this she told you that she did not want other people to hear what she thought. What is her most likely psychopathology?
questions.explanation: Thought broadcasting refers to the delusional belief that one's thoughts are known to others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following examples cannot be classified among first rank symptoms of schizophrenia?

options.text: Feeling of sunrays directed by US army satellites entering inside the knee, and causing the pain
Patient knew that he was the Wimbledon tennis champion when he saw the Wimbledon underground signboard
Voices asking the patient to go to London and meet the Queen
Voices commenting on the patient's actions

correct_answer.text: Voices asking the patient to go to London and meet the Queen

correct_answers.text: Voices asking the patient to go to London and meet the Queen

questions.explanation: This is an example of a command hallucination, which is not classified as a first rank symptom. It   may be seen in conditions such as schizophrenia and severe depression. Écho de la pensée is the   French term used for thought echo. Delusional perception and somatic passivity are also first rank   symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old alcohol-dependent man presents to the accident and emergency department due to a distressing sensation of little animals crawling over his body. What is this phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Haptic hallucinations involve sensations of touch and can manifest as the feeling of insects crawling on the skin.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old woman was in a hurry to catch the last train to Hertford. She was already late. However, in her hurry, she read Hereford as Hertford and boarded the train for Hereford. What is the most likely phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Completion illusion occurs when familiar letters or words are misread due to cognitive overload or haste.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old male inpatient refused to accept his medication. He said that his doctor is an imposter even though he acknowledged that he looks the same. What psychopathology does he have?
questions.explanation: Capgras' syndrome entails the delusion that a close person has been replaced by an identical impostor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not explain the process of 'forgetting'?
questions.explanation: Ineffective registration or encoding could be due to lack of attention, so information is not learned   in the first place. Decay refers to the fading of memory traces with time. The Interference theory   of forgetting proposes that people forget because of competition from other material learned   previously or subsequently. The tendency to forget things, i.e. one does not want to remember, is   motivated by forgetting which is similar to repression in freudian terms. Decoding is not described   in memory or forgetting

questions.question_text: A 47-year-old man was observed to be walking sideways along the hospital corridor. When asked for the reason, he said that it was 'because of the side effects'. Which of the following explains this observation?
questions.explanation: Concrete thinking refers to taking statements literally, resulting in misunderstandings about side effects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a narcissistic defence mechanism?
questions.explanation: Projection involves attributing one’s unacceptable impulses or feelings to others, which is common in narcissistic defense mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is associated with an ego defence mechanism of avoidance?
questions.explanation: Avoidance as a defense mechanism is typically seen in post-traumatic stress disorder where individuals avoid triggers related to trauma.

questions.question_text: What is the reservoir of feelings, thoughts, urges and memory that is outside our conscious awareness known as?
questions.explanation: The unconscious mind contains thoughts and feelings that are not currently accessible to conscious awareness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a narcissistic defence mechanism?
questions.explanation: Projection is a key defense mechanism in narcissism, where unwanted feelings are attributed to others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about a transitional object is correct?

options.text: Anna Freud used it to encourage transference in the analysis of children at play
It is commonly used by a child to manage anxiety
It is commonly used by people with learning disabilities to manage anxiety
It impedes a satisfactory progress of mourning
It was a concept first used by Melanie Klein

correct_answer.text: It is commonly used by a child to manage anxiety

correct_answers.text: It is commonly used by a child to manage anxiety

questions.explanation: Transitional objects help manage anxiety by providing comfort and security as the child learns independence.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man with schizophrenia presented with waxy flexibility. His psychiatrist diagnosed him as having catatonia. Who coined the term 'catatonia'?
questions.explanation: The term 'catatonia' was introduced by Kahlbaum to describe this specific state characterized by severe motor disturbances.

questions.question_text: In the 1960s, patients with schizophrenia improved after treatment with chlorpromazine. Who is associated with the introduction of chlorpromazine?
questions.explanation: Deniker is credited with introducing chlorpromazine as an effective treatment for schizophrenia in the 1950s.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man with schizophrenia heard voices commenting on his actions and believed that his actions were controlled by aliens. These are two of the first rank symptoms. Who was the first to propose it?
questions.explanation: Kurt Schneider was pivotal in defining the concept of first rank symptoms in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A 24-year-old young woman with a history of prominent mood changes presented with shallow mood, and inappropriate and disorganised thoughts. The onset is usually in adolescence with this type of schizophrenia. Who first described it?
questions.explanation: Hecker was one of the first to describe hebephrenic schizophrenia, characterized by disorganized thought processes and inappropriate affect.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old single man was going through a depressive episode of moderate severity. He mainly lacked interest in his daily activities and hobbies. His psychiatrist said that he had anhedonia. Who coined this term?
questions.explanation: The term 'anhedonia,' which refers to the inability to experience pleasure, was coined by Ribot.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man experienced his first episode of bipolar affective disorder–current episode mania. He was assessed by a psychiatrist who observed tangentiality and circumstantiality while speaking and described the symptoms as a formal thought disorder. Who proposed formal thought disorder for the first time?
questions.explanation: Kurt Schneider is known for his work on formal thought disorder in the context of psychotic disorders.

questions.question_text: Maslow's triangle represents the hierarchy of needs where, to reach the higher level, the lower level must be satisfied. In which year was this theory put forward?
questions.explanation: Maslow introduced his hierarchy of needs theory in 1943, emphasizing the progression of human motivation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs was introduced in 1967 as the first antipsychotic depot injection?
questions.explanation: Modecate (fluphenazine decanoate) was the first antipsychotic depot injection introduced in 1967.

questions.question_text: Who discovered the design of randomised controlled trials?
questions.explanation: Bradford Hill is recognized for pioneering the methodology of randomized controlled trials.

questions.question_text: Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) were discovered long before other antidepressants. Which of the following was the first TCA to be used?
questions.explanation: Imipramine was the first tricyclic antidepressant to be widely used, discovered in the 1950s.

questions.question_text: Who is associated with schizoaffective psychosis?
questions.explanation: Jacob Kasanin introduced the concept of schizoaffective disorder, blending features of schizophrenia and mood disorders.

questions.question_text: Who is associated with the treatment of mania with lithium?
questions.explanation: John Cade is credited with the discovery of lithium's effectiveness in treating manic episodes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about stigma and mental illness in the Indian subcontinent is false?

options.text: The person fears rejection by parents
Men suffer from stigma more often than women do, because they are breadwinners
The person needs to hide the condition from others
Older people are more stigmatised than young people
The stigma was related to fear of job prospects

correct_answer.text: The person needs to hide the condition from others

correct_answers.text: The person needs to hide the condition from others

questions.explanation: Older people tend to face less stigma compared to younger individuals regarding mental illness in Indian society.

questions.question_text: In terms of evidence of prejudice against mental illness, which of the following is correct?

options.text: People with mental illness provoke distaste or disgust in others
Most of the public are generally hostile towards people with mental illness
Most of the public resent people with mental illness
There is a fear of violence from people with mental illness
There is anger among the general population towards people with mental illness

correct_answer.text: There is a fear of violence from people with mental illness

correct_answers.text: There is a fear of violence from people with mental illness

questions.explanation: Common evidence shows that there is a notable fear of violence associated with mental illness, despite other negative perceptions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about locura is correct?

options.text: It is an acute psychotic illness with quick resolution
It is a dissociative state that follows acute trauma
It is a mild, psychotic, culture-bound syndrome
The condition is attributed to an inherited vulnerability
It resembles the negative symptoms of schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: The condition is attributed to an inherited vulnerability

correct_answers.text: The condition is attributed to an inherited vulnerability

questions.explanation: Locura is recognized as a culture-bound syndrome manifesting mild psychosis in certain cultural contexts.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is consistent with bouffée délirante?

options.text: It is not a classified syndrome in the ICD-10
It is not a culture-bound syndrome
It results in sudden and complete recovery within days
It is rarely seen in black people

questions.explanation: Bouffée délirante often leads to a rapid resolution of symptoms, typically within days.

questions.question_text: Ekbom's syndrome is a culture-bound syndrome. Which of the following statements describes it?

options.text: It is found in remote eastern countries
It is a monosymptomatic hypochondriacal psychosis
It mainly presents with a perceptual disturbance

correct_answer.text: It is a monosymptomatic hypochondriacal psychosis

correct_answers.text: It is a monosymptomatic hypochondriacal psychosis

questions.explanation: Ekbom's syndrome, also known as delusional parasitosis, is identified as a hypochondriacal psychosis involving beliefs about being infested with parasites.
